title: An Interaction Is All You Need — Ivan Leo, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: This is a Google DeepMind product launch talk for the Interactions API and managed anti-gravity agents, not a practitioner lesson. The transferable ideas are architectural primitives: server-side conversation state keyed by an interaction ID, persistent sandbox state keyed by an environment ID, and a credential-injecting MITM proxy for agent network calls.

takeaways.technique: Server-side state via opaque interaction ID
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of the client resending and reassembling full conversation history (including opaque thought signatures), the API returns an interaction ID; passing previous_interaction_id preserves all context and cache server-side.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as long as you give us back that same interaction ID under the parameter previous interaction ID ... all that context is preserved

takeaways.technique: Persistent sandbox keyed by environment ID
takeaways.what_they_do: A single API call boots a remote sandbox; returning the environment ID routes subsequent calls back to the same sandbox with installed packages and files intact, so state persists across turns without client-side management.
takeaways.evidence_quote: as long as you preserve the environment ID that we returned to you, you're able to route it right back to the original sandbox
takeaways.numbers: one run burned over two million tokens analyzing a repo

takeaways.what_they_do: All outbound agent calls pass through a proxy that inspects headers and injects real tokens (e.g., GitHub) so the model never sees the secret, even under prompt injection.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even if the model is somehow prompt injected and leaks your GitHub API token, it's never actually going to see the token

takeaways.technique: Package tuned skills as a portable folder
takeaways.what_they_do: Skills tuned locally in the IDE are packaged into a single folder and uploaded as sources, so the same harness, prompt, and skills run locally and in the cloud.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you just package it into a single folder ... that gives your agent the exact same skills with the same agent harness and the same prompt running locally and in the cloud

takeaways.what_they_do: Replaces deeply nested legacy output arrays with a steps model where each step has a tight discriminator (content type, tool call, signature), simplifying parsing of multimodal/async tool outputs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've introduced the steps data model which replaces the original legacy outputs array with a tight discriminator
